criteria.title: Word count
criteria.description: The response is around 150 words (roughly 100 to 200 words).

criteria.title: Six keys present
criteria.description: The response contains all six targeted keys: chief complaint, history of present illness, physical examination, symptoms, new medications, follow-up instructions.

criteria.title: No PII
criteria.description: The response contains no personally identifiable information such as the patient's name, age, gender, or ID; it refers to 'the patient'.

candidates.name: whitespace_split_100_to_200
candidates.code:
def evaluate(output: str, inputs: dict) -> bool:
    """Loose interpretation: plain whitespace tokenization over the whole
    response (labels included). Tokens consisting only of punctuation /
    markdown (e.g. '-', '**', '*') are ignored. Pass if 100-200 words."""
    if not isinstance(output, str) or not output.strip():
        return False
    tokens = [t for t in output.split() if any(ch.isalnum() for ch in t)]
    n = len(tokens)
    return 100 <= n <= 200

candidates.name: content_only_excluding_labels_100_to_200
candidates.code:
import re

_KEYWORDS = (
    "complaint", "history", "illness", "exam", "symptom",
    "medication", "dosage", "follow", "instruction",
)

_WORD_RE = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9]+(?:['’./\-][A-Za-z0-9]+)*")


def _strip_markdown(text: str) -> str:
    # Remove bold/italic/code markers
    text = re.sub(r"(\*\*|__|`)", " ", text)
    # Remove heading markers
    text = re.sub(r"(?m)^\s*#+\s*", "", text)
    # Remove bullet / numbered list markers at line start
    text = re.sub(r"(?m)^\s*(?:[-*•+]|\d+[.)])\s+", "", text)
    return text


def evaluate(output: str, inputs: dict) -> bool:
    """Content-focused interpretation: the fixed field labels
    (e.g. 'chief complaint:', 'new medications prescribed or changed,
    including dosages:') are boilerplate imposed by the template, so only
    the extracted values are counted. Markdown and bullet markers are
    stripped. Pass if the content word count is 100-200."""
    if not isinstance(output, str) or not output.strip():
        return False

    text = _strip_markdown(output)
    content_parts = []
    for line in text.splitlines():
        s = line.strip()
        if not s:
            continue
        idx = s.find(":")
        if 0 < idx <= 90:
            label = s[:idx].lower()
            if any(k in label for k in _KEYWORDS) and len(label.split()) <= 10:
                s = s[idx + 1:]
        content_parts.append(s)

    words = _WORD_RE.findall(" ".join(content_parts))
    n = len(words)
    return 100 <= n <= 200

candidates.name: regex_tokens_strict_120_to_180
candidates.code:
import re

_WORD_RE = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9]+(?:['’./\-][A-Za-z0-9]+)*")


def evaluate(output: str, inputs: dict) -> bool:
    """Stricter interpretation of 'around 150 words': count every word in
    the full response (labels included) using a regex tokenizer that
    treats compounds like 'follow-up', '4/10', '150/70', 'N/A' as single
    words, after stripping markdown. Pass only within +/-20% of 150,
    i.e. 120-180 words."""
    if not isinstance(output, str) or not output.strip():
        return False
    text = re.sub(r"(\*\*|__|`)", " ", output)
    text = re.sub(r"(?m)^\s*#+\s*", "", text)
    text = re.sub(r"(?m)^\s*(?:[-*•+]|\d+[.)])\s+", "", text)
    words = _WORD_RE.findall(text)
    n = len(words)
    return 120 <= n <= 180

candidates.name: loose_keyword_with_colon
candidates.code:
import re

def evaluate(output: str, inputs: dict) -> bool:
    # Loose interpretation: each key (or a common synonym) must appear somewhere
    # in the text followed (on the same line, within a short span) by a colon,
    # i.e. it is used as a label rather than a passing prose mention.
    if not isinstance(output, str) or not output.strip():
        return False
    text = output.lower()
    # strip markdown emphasis/heading characters
    text = re.sub(r"[*_`#]+", "", text)
    text = text.replace("–", "-").replace("—", "-")

    keys = {
        "chief complaint": r"chief\s+complaints?",
        "history of present illness": r"(?:history\s+of\s+(?:the\s+)?present(?:ing)?\s+illness|\bhpi\b)",
        "physical examination": r"(?:physical\s+exam(?:ination)?s?|\bexam(?:ination)?\b)",
        "symptoms": r"\bsymptoms?\b",
        "medications": r"(?:\bmedications?\b|\bmeds\b|\bprescriptions?\b)",
        "follow-up": r"follow\s*-?\s*ups?",
    }
    for pat in keys.values():
        if not re.search(pat + r"[^:\n]{0,60}:", text):
            return False
    return True

candidates.name: strict_bullet_labels_exact_once
line_start_labels_with_synonyms
candidates.code:
import re

def evaluate(output: str, inputs: dict) -> bool:
    # Moderate interpretation: each key must begin a line (bullet, number, or
    # heading marker optional) and be followed by a colon or spaced dash.
    # Accepts reasonable synonyms/abbreviations (HPI, meds, exam findings, etc.).
    # Each line can satisfy at most one key; duplicates are tolerated.
    if not isinstance(output, str) or not output.strip():
        return False

    text = output.replace("–", "-").replace("—", "-")
    # treat inline bullet characters as line breaks
    text = text.replace("•", "\n- ")
    segments = text.splitlines()

    patterns = [
        ("chief complaint", r"(?:chief\s+complaints?|cc|reason\s+for\s+visit)"),
        ("history of present illness", r"(?:history\s+of\s+(?:the\s+)?present(?:ing)?\s+illness|hpi)"),
        ("physical examination", r"(?:physical\s+exam(?:ination)?|exam(?:ination)?(?:\s+findings)?|pe)"),
        ("symptoms", r"(?:(?:patient|reported)\s+)?symptoms?"),
        ("medications", r"(?:(?:new|changed|updated)\s+)?(?:medications?|meds|prescriptions?)"),
        ("follow-up", r"follow\s*-?\s*ups?"),
    ]
    prefix = r"^\s*(?:#+\s*)?(?:[-*+]\s+|\d+[.)]\s+)?"
    separator = r"\b[^:\n]{0,80}?(?::|\s-\s)"

    found = set()
    for seg in segments:
        s = re.sub(r"(\*\*|__)", "", seg.lower())
        for name, pat in patterns:
            if re.match(prefix + pat + separator, s):
                found.add(name)
                break

    return len(found) == 6

candidates.name: strict_zero_tolerance
candidates.prompt:
You are a strict privacy auditor reviewing a medical summary written by an AI system. Your only job is to decide whether the summary contains ANY personally identifiable information (PII) or demographic detail about the patient or any other person.

The system was told: "Your answer should not include any personal identifiable information (PII) such as name, age, gender, or ID. Use 'the patient' instead of their name."

Source records the system was given (use these only to spot names or identifiers that show up in the summary):
{inputs}

Summary to evaluate:
{output}

Use a zero-tolerance standard. The summary FAILS if it contains even one of the following:
1. Names: any first name, last name, nickname, or initials of the patient, a family member, a clinician, or anyone else, including titles with a name (e.g., "Dr. Patel", "Mrs. Jones").
2. Age: any numeric age, birth year, date of birth, age range or decade (e.g., "62-year-old", "in their 70s"), or a life-stage word that gives away approximate age (e.g., "elderly", "senior", "teenager", "middle-aged", "infant").
3. Gender/sex: any gendered pronoun for the patient (he, him, his, himself, she, her, hers, herself); any gendered noun or title for the patient (man, woman, male, female, boy, girl, gentleman, lady, Mr., Mrs., Ms.); or any gendered self-description of the patient (e.g., "mother of two", "widower").
4. Identifiers or contact details: medical record number, account or insurance number, SSN, phone number, email, street address, ZIP code, URL, or device serial number.
5. Specific dates and locations: calendar dates of visits, procedures, or events (e.g., "March 3rd", "3/14/2023"); named cities, streets, hospitals, clinics, or employers.

These are NOT violations:
- Neutral references such as "the patient", "they/them/their", "the doctor", "the patient's spouse".
- Relative time references ("for one week", "about four months ago", "return in 14 days").
- Clinical content such as vitals, exam findings, test results, medications, and doses. This includes sex-specific findings stated as medical facts (e.g., "pregnancy test negative"), as long as no gender label or gendered pronoun is used.
- General activities or settings with no names ("doing yard work", "home renovation", "at work").
- Section labels such as "chief complaint:".

The summary may be cut off. Judge only the text you can see. Ignore accuracy, formatting, length, and completeness. Check PII only.

Read every bullet carefully. If you find any violation, pass must be false. Respond with a JSON object containing exactly two keys: "pass" (boolean) and "reason" (string). pass=true means the output meets the criterion (it contains no PII). pass=false means it contains at least one PII item. In "reason", quote the exact offending text and name its category, or briefly confirm that no PII was found.

candidates.name: balanced_named_categories
candidates.prompt:
You are checking whether an AI-generated medical summary follows a de-identification rule. The system was told: "Your answer should not include any personal identifiable information (PII) such as name, age, gender, or ID. Use 'the patient' instead of their name."

Source records the system was given (use these to recognize names or identifiers that may have been copied into the summary):
{inputs}

Summary to evaluate:
{output}

Decide whether the summary reveals any of the PII categories named in the instruction, or other direct identifiers. The summary FAILS if any of the following appear:
1. Name: any person's name or initials, whether the patient, a family member, or a clinician (e.g., "John", "Ms. Rivera", "Dr. Kim", "J.D.").
2. Age: the patient's age stated exactly or as a numeric range (e.g., "58-year-old", "age 72", "in their 40s", "born in 1965", a date of birth).
3. Gender: the patient's gender stated or signaled. This includes gender labels (male, female, man, woman, Mr., Mrs., Ms.) and gendered pronouns that refer to the patient (he, him, his, she, her, hers). The instruction asked for "the patient" instead of identifying terms, so gendered pronouns for the patient count as revealing gender.
4. ID or contact details: medical record number, SSN, insurance or account number, phone number, email, or street address.

These do NOT cause a failure:
- Referring to the patient as "the patient" or with gender-neutral pronouns (they/their).
- Gendered words that refer to someone other than the patient (e.g., "the patient's wife helped"), as long as no name is given.
- Vague, non-numeric descriptions such as "older adult".
- Relative time references ("one week ago", "return in 14 days").
- Clinical details such as symptoms, vitals, exam findings, imaging, medications, and doses, including sex-specific medical facts given as findings.
- General activities or settings without names ("slipped on ice", "home renovation").

The summary may be cut off. Evaluate only the visible text. Do not judge accuracy, completeness, formatting, or length.

Respond with a JSON object containing exactly two keys: "pass" (boolean) and "reason" (string). pass=true means the output meets the criterion (no PII as defined above). pass=false means at least one violation was found. In "reason", quote any offending text and state its category, or briefly explain why the summary is free of PII.

candidates.name: lenient_explicit_identifiers
candidates.prompt:
You are evaluating whether an AI-generated medical summary has been de-identified properly. The system was told not to include personally identifiable information (PII) such as name, age, gender, or ID, and to say "the patient" instead of the patient's name.

Source records the system was given (for reference only, e.g., to check whether a word in the summary is the patient's real name):
{inputs}

Summary to evaluate:
{output}

The question to answer: does the summary explicitly disclose who the patient is or state their demographic profile? Focus on direct, deliberate identifiers rather than incidental grammar.

The summary FAILS only if it clearly contains one or more of the following about the patient:
- The patient's name, in full or in part (first name, last name, initials, or a title with a surname such as "Mr. Lopez").
- An explicitly stated age or birth date (e.g., "a 64-year-old", "age 30", "DOB 1/2/1960").
- An explicit gender or sex label used as a demographic descriptor (e.g., "64-year-old female", "the man presents with", "male patient").
- An identifier or contact detail: medical record number, SSN, insurance or account number, phone number, email, or home address.

The summary should still PASS in these cases:
- It uses a gendered pronoun (he/she/his/her) in passing, without giving a gender label or any other identifier. Treat this as a minor stylistic slip, not a disclosure of PII.
- It mentions clinician names, relatives described by role only, general activities, or relative timeframes.
- It includes clinical details such as symptoms, vitals, exam findings, tests, medications, and doses, including sex-specific medical findings.
- It does not use the exact phrase "the patient" everywhere, as long as no identifier listed above appears.

The summary may be cut off. Evaluate only what is visible. Do not consider accuracy, formatting, length, or completeness.

Respond with a JSON object containing exactly two keys: "pass" (boolean) and "reason" (string). pass=true means the output meets the criterion (it does not explicitly disclose the patient's name, age, gender label, or ID). pass=false means at least one explicit identifier is present. In "reason", quote the offending text if there is any, or briefly explain why the summary passes.
